sn36.15:1.1: Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side, and said to him:
sn36.15:1.2: “Venerable sir, what now is feeling? What is the origin of feeling? What is the cessation of feeling? What is the way leading to the cessation of feeling?
sn36.15:1.3: What is the gratification in feeling? What is the danger? What is the escape?”
sn36.15:1.5: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling—
sn36.15:1.7: With the arising of contact there is the arising of feeling.
sn36.15:1.8: With the cessation of contact there is the cessation of feeling.
sn36.15:1.9: This Noble Eightfold Path is the way leading to the cessation of feeling; that is,
sn36.15:1.11: The pleasure and joy that arise in dependence on feeling: this is the gratification in feeling.
sn36.15:1.12: That feeling is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change: this is the danger in feeling.
sn36.15:1.13: The removal and abandonment of desire and lust for feeling: this is the escape from feeling.
sn36.15:1.14: “Then, Ānanda, I have also taught the successive cessation of formations … as in §11….
sn36.15:1.29: For a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, lust has been tranquillized, hatred has been tranquillized, delusion has been tranquillized.”
